note: Item wording, block intro texts and response anchors transcribed from the study's own OSF codebook (osf.io/zevcs, 'Codebook Personality Change Intervention Study.pdf', osf.io/download/ypkfn, sha256 92b44918902860a60ec0dfed87315db8999ad75d6b04cfd78a962154bff74ce1, pp.17-24, 'Self-acceptance: Pre' and 'Self-acceptance: Post'), which prints each item against its SoSci variable (SA05, SA06_01, SA07_01..15, SA01_01/02, SA14_01..15, SA04_01..03, SA12_01/02, SA16_01). Code derivation: data/personalitychange_kramer.py uses the source column names as item codes (the deposit .rda files, reproduce.zip sha256 e412511f24fcef642cd6f7c7410dfa6c9db8db3750a5cb8f148490d986be79fa, are already lowercase) -- no positional step. The .rda columns carry no variable/value labels (attributes NULL), so the tie is the codebook's explicit codes, hence paper_explicit. Live table reproduces the same-named .rda columns exactly: 40/40 items match per-item n, sum and sum of squares, each fingerprint unique among all sa* columns (verify script). The authors' clean_data_st1.R/st2.R comments independently restate the wording for sa06_01, sa01_01/02, sa12_01/02 and sa04_01..03 and the coding 1 = yes, 2 = no for sa05. Deviations: (1) the codebook's SA14 intro is wrapped in typographic quotation marks; they are dropped. (2) Anchors the codebook prints as a bare '2=' / '4=' (sa06_01, sa07_*, sa14_*) or '2='..'6=' (sa16_01) are unlabelled and ship with blank option_text. (3) sa05: the codebook reads 'Do you want to be better at accepting yourself?' while the authors' R comment reads '...accepting yourself for who you are?'; the codebook wording is shipped. (4) Items with no intro text in the codebook (sa05, sa06_01, sa01_*, sa12_*, sa16_01) share section _1 with a blank section_prompt; the three intro texts (SA07 pre facets, SA14 post facets, SA04 behaviour frequency) are section_prompts because they differ by block; instructions blank. Anchor direction corroborated from the deposit: sa06_01 mean 4.34 when sa05=1 (yes) vs 1.81/1.91 when sa05=2 (no), Studies 1/2; sa04 practice-frequency mean correlates +0.49/+0.34 with sa14 perceived-acceptance mean. Scope caveats (table, not text): sa12_01/02 were administered in Study 1 only and sa16_01 in Study 2 at T3 only (codebook note + script); sa07_* and sa14_* adjectives are the 15 BFI-2 facet labels, not BFI-2 items. note: Item wording and instructions transcribed verbatim from the study's own OSF codebook (osf.io/zevcs, 'Codebook Personality Change Intervention Study.pdf', osf.io/download/ypkfn, sha256 92b44918902860a60ec0dfed87315db8999ad75d6b04cfd78a962154bff74ce1, p.15), which prints each item against its SoSci variable SC01_01..SC01_12. Code derivation: data/personalitychange_kramer.py uses the source column names as item codes (sc01_01..sc01_12, the deposit .rda already lowercase) -- no positional step; the .rda columns carry no variable/value labels (attributes NULL), so the tie is the codebook's explicit codes, hence paper_explicit. ANCHOR OVERRIDE: the codebook lists '1 = Strongly disagree / 2 = / 3 = Neutral; no opinion / 4 = / 5 = strongly disagree'; the 5 anchor is a copy error (same typo in its RSES block) and ships as 'strongly agree'. Data confirm 5 = agree: in all three studies' raw .rda files the 10 low-clarity items correlate negatively with the SWLS mean (-0.18..-0.34; SWLS is fully labelled 1 = Strongly disagree..7 = Strongly agree) and sc01_11 ('clear sense of who I am') correlates +0.32/+0.38/+0.37. Anchors 2 and 4 are unlabelled in the source and ship blank. Live table equals the raw deposit (pooled per-item means identical, max diff 0), items stored raw, not reverse-scored; study's own keys (clean_data_st1.R) reverse all but sc01_06 and sc01_11. CAVEAT: sc01_06 ('I seldom experience conflict...'), canonically positive-keyed, correlates ~0 with SWLS (+0.02/+0.06/+0.00) and with the other items (+0.03/-0.04/+0.13 with the low-clarity mean) -- item behaviour, not a mapping or text issue.
